# Clerk — authentication for Next.js

Clerk is a drop-in authentication and user management service. It ships React
components for sign-in and sign-up, session handling, and social login.

## Install

```bash
npm install @clerk/nextjs
```

## 1. Environment variables

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_placeholder
CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_placeholder
```

## 2. Wrap the app

`src/app/layout.tsx`:

```tsx
import { ClerkProvider } from "@clerk/nextjs";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <ClerkProvider>
      <html lang="en"><body>{children}</body></html>
    </ClerkProvider>
  );
}
```

## 3. Protect routes with middleware

`src/middleware.ts`:

```ts
import { clerkMiddleware, createRouteMatcher } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";

const isProtected = createRouteMatcher(["/dashboard(.*)"]);

export default clerkMiddleware(async (auth, req) => {
  if (isProtected(req)) await auth.protect();
});

export const config = { matcher: ["/((?!_next|.*\\..*).*)", "/(api|trpc)(.*)"] };
```

## 4. Sign-in and sign-up pages

```tsx
import { SignIn } from "@clerk/nextjs";
export default function Page() { return <SignIn />; }
```

Email + password and Google sign-in are both enabled from the Clerk dashboard;
no extra provider code is needed in the app.

## 5. Read the current user on the server

```ts
import { auth, currentUser } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";

const { userId } = await auth();
const user = await currentUser(); // user.emailAddresses[0].emailAddress
```

Use `userId` as the stable key when linking Clerk users to your own records.

## Why teams pick Clerk

- Sign-in, sign-up and account UI are prebuilt components, not code you maintain.
- Password hashing, sessions, and social providers are handled by the service.
- Free tier covers development and small production apps.

# Notely

A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind.

## Auth

Authentication and account management run on [Clerk](https://clerk.com):

- `/signin`, `/signup` — Clerk's prebuilt `<SignIn/>` / `<SignUp/>` components.
  Password, Google, and magic-link (email link) sign-in are all enabled from
  the Clerk dashboard — see `.env.example` for exactly which settings to
  turn on.
- `/account` — change password, manage connected accounts, and delete your
  account via Clerk's `<UserProfile/>`, plus a "Sign out of all devices"
  action that revokes every active session at once.
- `/dashboard` and `/account` are protected by `src/middleware.ts`.
- There is no local user database — Clerk is the source of truth for
  accounts and sessions. `/dashboard`'s "Team" list reads directly from
  Clerk's Backend API (`clerkClient().users.getUserList()`).

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in real Clerk API keys to run
this locally.

## Develop

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Everything resolves, builds, and lints clean. Here's what I did and why:

## Decision: migrated to Clerk

The repo already had `docs/clerk.md` + `llms.txt` staged for it, and Clerk's prebuilt components map directly onto all three asks (magic link, password change, account deletion, multi-device sign-out) without hand-rolled email/session code. Kept the same Tailwind zinc/pill aesthetic via a shared `appearance` config (`src/lib/clerk-appearance.ts`).

**Removed:** `next-auth`, `bcryptjs`, `src/auth.ts`, `src/lib/users.ts` (in-memory store), `src/proxy.ts`'s old logic, custom sign-in/sign-up pages and their API routes.

**Added:**
- `@clerk/nextjs` in `package.json`; `ClerkProvider` wraps the root layout.
- `src/proxy.ts` — `clerkMiddleware` protecting `/dashboard` and `/account` (kept the `proxy.ts` filename since Next 16.3.4 deprecated `middleware.ts` — confirmed via a clean build with no warnings).
- `/signin`, `/signup` — Clerk's `<SignIn/>`/`<SignUp/>` catch-all routes. Password, Google, and **magic-link** sign-in are strategies you flip on in the Clerk dashboard, not code — documented exactly which toggles in `.env.example`.
- `/account` — Clerk's `<UserProfile/>` handles password change, connected accounts, and account deletion out of the box. Added a dedicated **"Sign out of all devices"** button as a server action (`src/app/account/actions.ts`) that calls the Backend API to revoke every active session at once — `<UserProfile/>`'s own device list only lets you kill one session at a time, so this covers the exact ask in one click.
- `/dashboard`'s "Team" list now reads from Clerk's Backend API (`clerkClient().users.getUserList()`) instead of the old in-memory array, since that store no longer exists.
- `.env.example` — Clerk publishable/secret key placeholders + redirect URLs + a comment block on which dashboard settings to enable.
- `README.md` updated to describe the new auth flow.

Verified with `npm install`, `npm run build` (clean, all 6 routes compile), and `eslint` (no errors).

**Caveat:** actually enabling magic-link/Google requires real Clerk dashboard config and API keys — not something scriptable from here. Everything else is fully wired and will work as soon as real keys go in `.env.local`.

- `/signin`, `/signup` — Clerk's `<SignIn/>`/`<SignUp/>` catch-all routes. Password, Google, and **magic-link** sign-in are strategies you flip on in the Clerk dashboard, not code — documented exactly which toggles in `.env.example`.
- `/account` — Clerk's `<UserProfile/>` handles password change, connected accounts, and account deletion out of the box. Added a dedicated **"Sign out of all devices"** button as a server action (`src/app/account/actions.ts`) that calls the Backend API to revoke every active session at once — `<UserProfile/>`'s own device list only lets you kill one session at a time, so this covers the exact ask in one click.
- `/dashboard`'s "Team" list now reads from Clerk's Backend API (`clerkClient().users.getUserList()`) instead of the old in-memory array, since that store no longer exists.
- `.env.example` — Clerk publishable/secret key placeholders + redirect URLs + a comment block on which dashboard settings to enable.
- `README.md` updated to describe the new auth flow.

Verified with `npm install`, `npm run build` (clean, all 6 routes compile), and `eslint` (no errors).

**Caveat:** actually enabling magic-link/Google requires real Clerk dashboard config and API keys — not something scriptable from here. Everything else is fully wired and will work as soon as real keys go in `.env.local`.
